# How to use NPRI Excel single year tabular data - ECCC

> **Provenance note:** This file comes from the publisher's web page (canada.ca), not from Brightspace. Verbatim retrieval was not possible through the available fetch tool (it returned a detailed paraphrase only), so the text below is a faithful point-by-point **paraphrase of the published transcript**. It is not verbatim.

1. Go to the NPRI website (Canada.ca/NPRI).
2. In the "Most requested" box on the right, click "Explore data".
3. Scroll to "Download NPRI Data" and click "Single year tables".
4. Choose a format: Excel (XLSX) or CSV, offered for the most recent three years.
5. The presenter uses the 2017 Excel file and clicks "Access"; the browser may ask to open or save.
6. The file holds the most commonly used NPRI data.
7. Row 4 holds the column headings, starting with year, NPRI ID# and company name.
8. Each following row is one substance report from one facility.
9. To the right: geographic data, sector descriptions, substance names.
10. Further right: quantities released to air, water and land; on-site and off-site disposal; off-site transfers for
    recycling.
11. Sort/filter with the arrows in heading row 4.
12. Example - Ottawa facilities: City heading arrow, uncheck "select all", select Ottawa.
13. Example - air releases: Total Air Emissions column arrow > "Sort Smallest to Largest" (caution: units differ
    between substances).
14. Example - nitrogen oxides: Substance Name arrow, uncheck "select all", select nitrogen oxides -> Ottawa facilities
    reporting NOx air releases, sorted.
15. Remove all filters/sorting: Data tab > "Clear".
16. Before interpreting, read "Using and Interpreting NPRI Data" (linked from the NPRI home page).

Course relevance: the course's `NPRI-INRP_DataDonnées_2024.csv` is the CSV version of this single-year table (see
[../../datasets/npri.md](../../datasets/npri.md)); the course's own Excel videos use Power Query instead of sheet filters.
